maria_cust: hey team — started getting 401 invalid_api_key for our prod requests after key rotation last night. Example curl:
curl -i -H "Authorization: ApiKey rk_live_a1b2c3...9zY=" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
Response: {"error":"invalid_api_key","status":401}
We rotate keys via HashiCorp Vault with KMS envelope encryption. Any ideas?

emma_support: thanks — can you paste the first/last 8 chars of the key, and the x-request-id from the HTTP response headers? Also did you rotate the Cloud KMS key used to unwrap the Vault secret around that time?

maria_cust: key starts "rk_live_a1b2c3" and ends "8y9zY==". x-request-id is req_0a1b2c3. yes we rotated the KMS key at 02:12 UTC.

raj_engineering: KMS rotation may cause Vault transit ciphertext to be unreadable if the rewrap step didn't run. Do Vault logs show anything like "invalid ciphertext" or "bad decrypt"? Also does the same key work against dev/staging?

maria_cust: dev/staging work fine. From Vault we see: 
```
error: invalid ciphertext: failed to decrypt with key version 1
```
So looks like decryption failed.

raj_engineering: that's consistent. Many teams see a placeholder or truncated value when a decrypt fails, which then makes requests present an invalid key and return 401. Can you run on the instance: `sudo cat /etc/secrets/redwood_apikey | xxd -b | head -n1` and paste the output? looking for trailing newline or NULs.

maria_cust: output: `01110010 01101011 01101100 01101001 01110110 01100101 01011111 ... 00101010` (base64 payload looks truncated, ends with newline). Also KMS new key id is projects/xyz/locations/global/keyRings/ring/cryptoKeys/new-key/cryptoKeyVersions/2

emma_support: two quick paths: 1) short-term: create a temporary API key from the Redwood Console and update the instance env var (fast patch) 2) longer-term: rewrap the Vault ciphertext with the new KMS key so decrypts succeed. We can walk you through rewrap if you have vault transit/rewrap perms.

sre_oliver: I'll help. @maria_cust, do we have a service account with roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter on the new key? If not, rewrap will fail. If you prefer we can issue a temporary key while you fix IAM.

maria_cust: can you share the rewrap steps? we have vault admin access but haven't run rewrap before.

raj_engineering: steps we've used (adapt to your env):
1) export CIPHERTEXT=$(vault kv get -field=apikey secret/redwood)
2) REWRAPPED=$(vault write -field=ciphertext transit/rewrap/new-key ciphertext=$CIPHERTEXT)
3) vault kv put secret/redwood apikey="$REWRAPPED"
That re-encrypts the ciphertext under the transit/new-key key and stores it back. Validate by fetching and attempting decrypt locally before rotating services.

emma_support: I'll generate a short-lived API key and DM it to you now so you can patch prod while SRE runs rewrap.

vault-bot: Incident created INC-1234 — temporary-key-issued, assigned to @emma_support, @sre_oliver

maria_cust: applied the temp key and prod calls are green again. thank you!! please proceed with the rewrap and confirm once IAM perms are ok. :thumbsup:

sre_oliver: on it — will update INC-1234 when rewrap + perms validated.

emma_support: marking follow-up: docs checklist for KMS rotation + test rewrap in staging to avoid this. cc @raj_engineering
